details: Bitcoin is currently trading near $81,500, exhibiting mixed technical indicators as it approaches the weekly close. The cryptocurrency is on track for its second consecutive week of losses, and the anticipated "uptober" trend has not materialized. Recent data indicates spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) experienced outflows of approximately $146.2 million this week. While a Bloomberg analyst warns Bitcoin could drop to $10,000 if U.S. stocks fall 20%, other analysts point to strong ETF inflows (totaling $58 billion absorbed) and on-chain data suggesting a floor closer to $30,000. The broader crypto market reflects caution and struggling demand.
title: Bitcoin Faces Headwinds Amid Mixed Technicals and ETF Outflows

details: Cardano (ADA) experienced a significant 14.6% price drop in the week leading up to October 17, 2026, marking the steepest decline among 26 large cryptocurrencies and substantially outpacing Bitcoin's 2.4% decrease. Traders are now closely monitoring the critical $0.20 support level. This underperformance follows an announcement by Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson that future Input Output products will not automatically launch on Cardano first, potentially removing a key catalyst for recovery.
title: Cardano Plunges Over 14%, Eyes Critical $0.20 Support Level

details: Google's new Willow quantum chip has significantly reduced errors in preparing "magic states," a crucial step in quantum computing that could eventually enable the breaking of Bitcoin wallet security. The chip achieved approximately 99.99% fidelity in these states. While this breakthrough improves the efficiency of quantum attacks by reducing hardware bottlenecks, it does not make Bitcoin attacks immediately cheaper. The development highlights the ongoing vulnerability of older Bitcoin wallets with exposed public keys to future quantum attacks, underscoring the need for enhanced cryptographic protections.
title: Google's Quantum Chip Advances Potential Long-Term Threat to Bitcoin Security

details: Michael Saylor's Strategy firm, a major corporate holder of Bitcoin, has indicated that it may purchase more of the cryptocurrency. This follows the company's disclosure that it now holds 848,250 BTC. Earlier in October, Strategy reported buying an additional 250 BTC between October 5 and October 11, spending approximately $215 million at an average cost of $86,194 per Bitcoin, including fees and expenses.
title: Michael Saylor Hints at Further Bitcoin Acquisitions After Disclosing Holdings

details: As the cryptocurrency market matures, altcoins are undergoing increased scrutiny regarding their utility. Research from early 2026 revealed that 53% of tokens tracked from mid-2021 through 2025 had already failed. Ethereum and Solana are highlighted for demonstrating real use cases, evidenced by their significant transaction fees and stablecoin activity. In contrast, altcoins like Cardano, Dogecoin, and Shiba Inu are noted for still needing to prove their investment thesis. For example, Cardano's investment thesis remains largely about future adoption, with relatively low value locked in its DeFi applications.
title: Altcoins Face Scrutiny: Ethereum & Solana Show Use Cases, Others Struggle
